findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The walk-in cooler shelves are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. Discussed cleaning them with the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There are mouse droppings observed to be in multiple areas throughout the dry storage area in the basement. These areas include, but are not limited to, a metal bowl, a metal container, on the lid of a rice cooker, on a plastic bag, and in ceramic bowls. An employee was shown these areas and where the mouse droppings are. It was discussed to make sure that all equipment that is brought upstairs to be used is washed, rinsed, and sanitized before use. A follow up will occur on 2/9/2026 to ensure that these mouse droppings have been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The cooler by the hostess stand was observed to have an ambient temperature of 60F. An employee had turned up the thermostat to defrost the back of the cooler. This cooler contained half & half and egg rolls. The half & half was voluntarily discarded and the egg rolls had recently been placed in there and were moved to another cooler. The facility has other coolers that can be utilized for cold holding. Only non-TCS food items remained in the cooler. Ensure that all TCS food items are moved to another functioning cooler before defrosting. A spot check will occur at the 1/30/2026 follow up to ensure that if the cooler is holding TCS food items that it is properly cold holding at 41F or under.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT- There was salmon in reduced oxygen packaging in the top of the preparation cooler that was observed to still be in its original packaging. The label and packaging states to remove from packaging prior to thawing. Proper thawing procedures were discussed with the staff. Reduced oxygen packaged salmon needs to be removed from the packaging or have the packaging cut before it can be thawed. Thawing should only be done through refrigeration, the cooking process, or under cold running water to prevent bacteria growth. CORRECTED- All packages of reduced oxygen packaged salmon that were thawed or currently being thawed had their package cut. Ensure that staff are educated on proper thawing procedures. This will be spot checked at the 1/30/2026 follow up.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: The probe thermometer in the facility recently broke and there is not another one available. A follow up is scheduled for 1/30/2026 to ensure that a probe thermometer has been obtained. Ensure that there is always a probe thermometer that is readily accessible in the facility to make sure that food is at the correct temperature.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There was a dead baby mouse on a glue trap observed to be in the basement under a shelf in the dry storage area. There were also mouse droppings observed to be in a bowl, on a box, and on a tote in the dry storage area as well. This was discussed with the PIC. A follow up will take place on 1/30/2026 to ensure that all mouse droppings have been cleaned up and that there is no evidence of mice or other rodents.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: REPEAT- There was a package of raw bacon on the top shelf above containers of cut vegetables in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- An employee moved the bacon below the vegetables and in the proper storage order. Proper storage order was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: REPEAT- There was salmon in reduced oxygen packaging in the top of the preparation cooler and on a shelf by the cook line that was observed to still be in its original packaging. The label and packaging states to remove from packaging prior to thawing. The packages of salmon that were on the shelf by the cook line were observed to be being thawed at room temperature. Proper thawing procedures were discussed with the staff. Reduced oxygen packaged salmon needs to be removed from the packaging or have the packaging cut before it can be thawed. Thawing should only be done through refrigeration, the cooking process, or under cold running water to prevent bacteria growth. CORRECTED- The salmon that was being thawed at room temperature was moved to the cooler (it had only been out for an hour) and all packages of reduced oxygen packaged salmon that were thawed or currently being thawed had their package cut. Ensure that staff are educated on proper thawing procedures.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: Two boxes of clear plastic lids are observed to be located on the floor in the side room. Take care to store single use items at least six inches above the floor. Boxes were taken to the basement for proper storage. 

(A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a large bag of sugar, container of oil and containers of juice stored on the floor inside of the back door. Provide an elevated surface on the other side of the door to keep food elevated 6 inches above the floor. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

Inspector observed items including phones, keys and wallets in various placed throughout the establishment kitchen. Provide a single place for storage of employee belongings.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 
Observed employee take a bottled drink from the glass front personal cooler, open and drink it in the wait station and then place the bottle on the counter holding clean dishes. The bottle was removed to the proper storage area for personal items. Employee was coached on the need to keep personal items and items for serving the public separated.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 
Observed the wall and area around the ansul system to be soiled with dust. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

(REPEAT) Observed employee to turn off faucets without barrier after washing hands correctly. Ensure a barrier such as a paper towel is utilized to turn off faucets after appropriately washing and drying hands - reduce cross contamination of hands. Discussed with PIC/employee. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/24/22.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the basement ice machine interior baffle to have mold. Ice machine needs cleaned - wash, rinse, sanitize. Ensure frequent cleaning of the interior of the ice machine to prevent mold build-up (food-contact surface). Inspector will follow-up on 9/2/22.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

Observed the lactic acid spray bottle to have too high of a concentration of the agent. Inspector’s utilized SCDPH test strips and the facility test strips. Both tested too high - 2258 and 3010 ppm. The product is not functioning appropriately. Discard. Utilize the bleach bucket (used in the kitchen) for the surfaces at the server station and in the dining area. Lactic acid is being used in predominantly those areas. Contact the distributor to discuss the issue. Inspector will follow-up on 8/26/22.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. 

Observed the seal at the exterior door (going down towards the basement) to not be secure. Light can be seen shining through at the bottom. Observed a very large cockroach near this door and headed towards the trim/broken seal of the exterior door. An appropriate seal is needed to prevent pests. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed a very large cockroach near the exterior door (going down towards basement). See attached photo page. No other roaches were observed in the basement or other pests/pest droppings. The basement is relatively dark and flash lights were used to look under dry storage and chest freezers. Orkin is used for pest control service per notes and routinely services once a month. Orkin should be called ASAP to address the cockroach situation. Inspector will follow-up on 9/2/22.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed multiple areas where dirty rags are on the floor under places: under the fryer/cook line, under freezers in the basement, next to the fryers. These rags were dirty to the point they should be discarded, not laundered. Ensure staff regularly going around the facility (including the basement) and throws out dirty rags. Dirty rags may be contributing to the pest (cockroach) situation. Discussed with PIC.

(REPEAT) Observed rags being utilized with the lactic acid spray bottle. Ensure paper towels or disposable towels are utilized to wipe surfaces instead of in-use rags. Cannot submerge rags in the lactic acid spray bottle. Discussed with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/24/22.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the gasket of the top freezer (refrigerator/freezer next to prep table along the prep line) to be broken. Duct tape is being used to hold it in place. Remove the duct tape and repair the gasket/seal of the freezer. Ensure equipment is maintained in good repair. Repair before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be in need of cleaning:
1. The racks above the 3 compartment sink are soiled in sticky residue. PIC indicated the racks need replaced and have tried to be cleaned before unsuccessfully. Replace before next routine inspection.
2. The dish machine has a build-up on lime. De-lime the dish machine (look at the interior side paneling specifically).
3. The fry/grill/cook line is in need of deep cleaning. Fryers/equipment should be moved out and the flooring under needs throughly cleaned of grease and food splash. 
(REPEAT) 4. The hood system has a large accumulation of grease. Advance Hood Cleaning Services serviced the system on 7/22/22 per the sticker on the hood. Next cleaning is 10/22. Service comes 4x yearly. Facility needs to spot clean in-between services since the company comes quarterly already. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/24/22.
5. The reach-in freezer in the basement has frozen food splash and debris at the base of the freezer. Clean the freezer.
6. All freezers in the basement (4) have a large amount of debris and rags under them. Pull them away from the wall and clean under the freezers.
7. Area under the dish machine has an accumulation of food debris and soil residue - clean area.

Ensure routine cleaning of non-food contact areas. Dedicate a cleaning day for staff in order to maintain cleanliness. Wash, rinse, sanitize all areas. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the ceiling near the dish machine area to have water damage from a leak in the roof. Dry wall and caulking is deteriorating. This has been a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 12/7/21 and 3/24/22.

PIC indicated that there is a leak in the roof and it is causing further damage to the area and other ceiling areas of the facility. Repairs have been made to the roof and PIC is waiting for a heavy rain to see if the repaired roof has been successful. PIC did not want to repair the ceiling only to have further roof leaking damage.

The ceiling above the mop area has exposed insulation and missing dry wall - repair. This can cause pest control issues.

The ceiling next to the walk-in cooler (near the prep area where the reach-in freezer is in the kitchen) is also started to fray from water damage. Water damage is starting to occur above the prep line as well.

Repairs should be conducted to the roof and subsequently the ceiling in the kitchen areas/mop sink area where visible damage has occurred. The City of Springfield Building and Zoning has been contacted after discussing with Food Program Manager, CK. See attached photo page. Repair before next routine inspection (December 2022).

Other areas of the facility in need of physical facility repairs:
1. Mop sink has a large accumulation of black mold on the Nudo board and caulking around the sink. Replace the Nudo board and caulking. Scrub the basin of the mop sink as best as possible to reduce the black mold build-up.
2. The exterior door (going down toward the basement) needs new coving/trim/caulking. Coving is missing between the floor and the wall in this area. No caulking observed. A large cockroach attempted to crawl into the trim next to the exterior door during the inspection (roach was killed by Inspector). Seal the entire area tightly to prevent pests. 
3. Caulking at the sink (where the crock pot with sweet and sour sauce is sitting in - not used as a sink) at the server station is needed - moldy - re-caulk.
4. Duct tape was noted to be holding the gasket of the top freezer (refrigerator/freezer next to prep cooler along prep line). Duct tape is not an approved material. Remove and repair gasket/seal. 

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee to wash hands then turn off faucets without a barrier such as a paper towel. Ensure proper hand washing techniques - wash hands with soap and hot water, dry hands with paper towel, turn off faucets with paper towel, discard paper towel. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

(REPEAT) Observed sani bucket in the kitchen to have low concentration of bleach - 0 ppm. PIC added more bleach. Ensure bleach concentration is regularly checked and sani buckets changed. COS - 200 ppm. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/7/21.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed improper thawing of shrimp in the prep sink. Shrimp were not completely submerged under running water. Discussed with employee who was thawing the shrimp. COS.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.citation_text:

Reference 3-501.14.

Chicken will be rapidly reheated to 165F and hot held at 135°F  or greater. PIC states chicken will be used by dinner service between 4:00-5:00 PM. Education provided. This is a repeat violation for the 2019 inspection year.

PIC states items are held on counter from 11:00 AM until 2:00 PM during lunch service, then placed back in cooler after lunch. Fried tofu and diced tomatoes were discarded during inspection. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed dishwasher to reach 132F. However, no sanitizer was present in machine. Corrected. Employee fixed issue. Cl- 100ppm. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment: Observed chicken to be 100F in cooling process in walk-in cooler.  According to PIC, chicken had been cooled since ~1430. Corrective Action. Chicken will be rapidly reheated to 165F and recooled with proper method. Education provided. Reference 3-501.14.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed chicken and pork to be out of temperature in prep cooler (T). These were probed at 56F and 46F respectively. Ensure proper cold holding occurs for all cold-held TCS foods. Corrective action. PIC stated products were placed in prep (T) around noon(1200). Products will be cooked and sold within six hours or discarded. Repair prep cooler. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed large pans being used in facility to cool products. Ensure proper cooling equipment is used to cool foods. This includes shallow pans, small amounts of food placed in containers, ice, ice wands, and other cooling methods. Implement new cooling methods to ensure adequate cooling. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Observed several dead roaches in downstairs area. Ensure remains of insects and any other pests are removed from premise in timely manner. Reference 6-501.112.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Lidded employee beverage observed on top shelf above food items such as spices, nuts, rice and clean utensils located on dry storage shelving across from the walk-in cooler

Please storage employee beverages in a manner to prevent contamination from food, food preparation areas, and clean utensils. Use lid and straw for employee beverages. Reference 2-401.11.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The following items were found improperly cold holding above 41F:

Following items noted stored at room temperature on countertop across from cookline: cut tomatoes 49F, large container of spouts 44F-48F, cooked tofu 45F. Items were placed into ice bath at the time of inspection. PIC indicated items are usually used during lunch rush, however leftovers are move back into cold holding. Discussed importance of keeping cold foods below 41F. Discussed using ice baths of obtaining a countertop cold holding unit.

In sliding door cooler on the server side of the pass thru window: (TOP) lettuce/noodle spring rolls 66F,  (BOTTOM) half and half 45F. Ambient temperature of top 50F-51FF, ambient temperature of bottom 45F.  Spring rolls were moved into proper cold holding unit. 

-> Cold held food items must be maintained below 41F for proper food safety. If using ice baths, ensure products are fully submerged in ice. Do not leave food out at room temperature without means of proper cold holding temperatures. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
The following food items were found without a proper date mark:
In the one door refrigerator next to rice cooker: cooked wide noodles, rice dessert, duck sauce, panag sauce, stuffed chicken buns, cut lettuce

In the walk-in cooler: tomato slices, wide noodles, rehydrated vermincelli noodles, cut cabbage and carrot mixture, crab cream cheese filling, masa sauce

* Staff indicated items have a prep date of 2-3 days. 

->Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded. Food is to be maintained at 41F or less and discarded after 7 days . Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Unlabeled bottle of degreaser found stored on shelf near the mop sink. Bottle was labeled at the time of inspection. 
Bottle of Alieve was noted stored above clean dishes located on shelf above clean drainboard at dish machine. 
2 bottles of WD-40 noted stored on shelf above 3 compartment sink and above clean preparation table. 

->Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.
->Medicines that are in a food establishment for the employees' use must be labeled as specified under 7-101.11 and located to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles. Removed by employee. Reference 7-207.11.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Internal thermometer not provided in front sliding door cooler on the server station side of the pass thru window. 

->Ambient air/water thermometer must be provided in all temperature holding units to assist in temperaure monitoring. Must be accurate to ±3°F in the intended range of use. Reference 4-203.12.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Panda brand Oyster Sauce noted open and stored in original can located on dry storage sheving unit near the walk-in cooler. 

->Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it in a food grade container and in a manner to protect from splash, dust or other contamination. Do not store food in opened original can. Reference 3-305.11.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Damp wiping cloths were noted stored at room temperature on preparation tables throughout the kitchen and on the bar cart in the service area by the pass thru window. 

->Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Heavy ice build-up noted on condenser in 3 door cooler across from the cookline. 
Bottom shelf under clean dish drainboard at dish machinenoted covered in cardboard. Bottom shelf of long island preparation table located in back kitchen noted lined with plastic liner. Liner observed soiled with sticky grease substance, soilage, and dried food debris. Clean utensils noted stored on both shelves.

-> Cardboard is not recognized as a safe material for food-contact and is being used to line or cover parts or all of a food-contact surface.  Provide materials that are safe, durable, corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and are smooth to allow for easy cleaning. Keep plastic liners clean of contamination. Reference 4-101.11.
